note: Item counts established by looking at each photograph with every proposal numbered on it, and judging each one. Only photographs where a person can actually count are here. On a dense Trader Joe's haul or a filled trolley the true number is not knowable from the image, and guessing at it would produce a metric with no ground under it.
counted_by: manual review of numbered overlays, one pass, re-done against the proposals the current detector prompt produces
product: one purchasable unit. A twin-pack of peanut butter is two jars because they are sold and scanned as two; a six-pack of ale is one carrier because it is sold as one. A napkin holder is not a product.

counted.note: Tofu, whole chilli, rice noodles, wasabi, ginger, mango: six proposals, six items, one each. The seventh item, a tied bunch of spring onions lying across the front of the table, drew nothing. Recounted against the current prompt; under the shape-word prompt this photograph was a clean seven of seven, and the item it now loses is loose produce.

Two Skippy jars, hummus tub, sun-dried tomato dip, bananas. Nine proposals: all five items found, plus a napkin holder that is not a product and three boxes drawn around parts of items already proposed.

Sambazon carton, Clover yogurt tub, a six-pack of Bigfoot ale as one carrier, a small blue bottle: four clean proposals. A fifth box spans both a decorative vase and the Rodney Strong bottle behind it, so the wine is covered but not isolated; counted as found on the same rule used throughout, which is whether a real product is covered by any proposal. Two oranges sitting in the middle of the group drew nothing at all.

Perdue ground turkey tray and one ShopRite deli bag proposed. The second ShopRite bag lying beside it, near-identical and fully visible, drew no proposal at all. Two proposals for three items: the first undercount in this set, and the first case of an item being missed rather than an extra one invented.

A produce haul laid out flat on a table with nothing behind anything, which is the easiest counting case in the corpus. Seven proposals, all seven correct: meat pack, grape bag, paper bag, bread bag, cauliflower, clementine bag, apple bag. Six items drew nothing: celery, parsley, a leek bunch, a parsnip, a net bag of onions and a net bag of potatoes. Every one of the six is loose or netted produce, and every one of the seven found is packaged. Not a hard-image problem.

Eight proposals for eight products, so the total is right, but not item for item. One proposal is the napkin holder, which is not a product; one product, a flour-tortilla packet standing behind the round tortillas, drew nothing. A count that is correct because two errors cancelled is the reason this file records `correct` separately from `products`.

recounted: `correct` depends on the proposals and therefore on the detector prompt; `products` does not, being a fact about the photograph. All six entries were re-judged against the current prompt. The first three were originally counted under the shape-word prompt and two of them changed.
rule: `correct` counts real products covered by at least one proposal. A proposal on a non-product does not subtract from it; it shows up as `proposed` exceeding `correct`.
missed_field: Each item the detector drew nothing for, and what kind of thing it is. Recorded per item rather than summarised so the pattern can be recounted when the detector changes, instead of being re-argued from prose.
